senses.gloss: (b. h., v. Ges. H. Dict. s. v.) [to rule,]

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 2:2">Snh. II, 2</cite> <he>המלך לא דָן ולא דָנִין וכ׳</he> the king must not act as judge, nor be summoned before court.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 82a:3">B. Kam. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>ודנין בשני וב׳</he> court is held on Mondays and Thursdays.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5">Snh. VII, 5</cite> <he>דנין את העדים וכ׳</he> witnesses are examined &c., v. <cite ref="K00566"><he>כִּינּוּי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 5a:10">Ib. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>ידין ידין</he> dare he hold court? He dare; a. fr.
<cite ref="Pesachim 27b:10">Pes. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>דָּנוּ דִין אחר</he> they argued differently.

<cite ref="Mishnah Maaser Sheni 2:9">Maas. Sh. II, 9</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 1:10">Eduy. I, 10</cite> <he>הַדָּנִין לפני חכמים</he> those who argued before the scholars; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 17b:10">Snh. 17ᵇ</cite> by ‘those who argued &c.’ are meant R. Shimeon &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:5">Ab. Zar. III, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 45a:4">45ᵃ</cite>) <he>אני אובין ואָדוּן</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 8), v. <cite ref="B00635"><he>בִּין</he></cite>.
R. Hash. 7ᵃ דנין שנה … משנה וכ׳ we compare the word shanah (year), used in connection with months, with shanah used &c. (Num. XXVIII, 14 with Ex. XII, 2); a. fr.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:6">Ab. I, 6</cite>, v. <cite ref="G00452"><he>זְכוּת</he></cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: נָדוֹן) to be judged, be called to account, summoned, punished, sentenced.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:2">R. Hash. I, 2</cite> <he>העולם נ׳</he> sentence is passed upon the world (prosperity or failure decreed).

Ib. 16ᵃ נִידּוֹנֶת לשעבר sentence has been passed upon it in the previous year (on the Passover, before the seed was sown), נ׳ להבא on the Passover of this same year (after the seed has been planted).
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 16a:13">Ib.</cite> <he>אדם נ׳ בכל יום</he> judgment is passed on man every day.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 12a:4">Ib. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>ברותחין נִידּוֹנוּ</he> they were punished with (found their death in) hot water.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:15">Ab. III, 15</cite> <he>בטוב העולם נ׳</he> the world is ruled with divine mercy.
<cite ref="Chullin 45a">Ḥull. 45ᵃ</cite> <he>נ׳ כמוח</he> is subject to the same law as the brain.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 2:5">B. Kam. II, 5</cite> <he>להיות כנ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00444"><he>דַּי</he></cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 2:8">Koh. R. to II, 8</cite> <he>היתה מְדַיֶּינֶת וכ׳</he> she argued (contended) with him.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 2:8">Ib.</cite> <he>שמְדַיְּינִין בהלכה</he> who argue legal questions.—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 3:6">Gen. R. s. 3</cite> <he>היו מדיינין זה עם זה</he> contended with one another; a. fr.
